title: Gap Preserving Distillation by Building Bidirectional Mappings with A Dynamic Teacher

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The purpose of the contribution is to mitigate the issue where a large performance gap between teacher and student models in knowledge distillation (KD) hinders training, by maintaining a reasonable performance gap throughout the training process. This purpose is explicitly addressed in [1] ("as the capacity gap between students and teachers becomes larger, existing KD methods fail to achieve better results") and [3] ("the performance gap between the teacher and student networks can affect the student's training"). Both papers aim to address the same problem of mitigating the negative effects of a large teacher-student performance gap in KD.

### Mechanism
The mechanism involves introducing a dynamically trained teacher (Dynamic Teacher, DT) that is co-trained with the student to act as a proxy, converting the problem of "determining the optimal gap" into "constructing an appropriate model size gap" and dynamically maintaining the teacher-student performance gap during each iteration. This mechanism is not directly equivalent to any prior paper. While [1] proposes dynamic prior knowledge (DPK) by integrating part of the teacher's features, and [3] uses dynamic entropy correction to adjust the student, neither introduces a co-trained dynamic teacher as a proxy to maintain a performance gap. Similarly, [9] introduces a teacher assistant to bridge the gap but does not dynamically co-train a teacher proxy. Thus, the mechanism appears novel.

### Evaluation
The evaluation involves demonstrating consistent improvements on ImageNet by combining the proposed method with existing KD methods, showing accuracy gains such as a 1.01% improvement for ResNet34→ResNet18 and a 1.58% improvement for ResNet50→MobileNet. This evaluation design — using ImageNet as a benchmark and reporting accuracy improvements for specific teacher-student pairs — is standard in KD research. For example, [1], [3], and [9] all evaluate their methods on ImageNet or similar benchmarks, reporting accuracy improvements for specific teacher-student pairs. Therefore, the evaluation design is covered.

### Domain
The domain is computer vision, specifically knowledge distillation and model compression. This domain is extensively covered by prior work, including [1], [3], [9], and many others, which all focus on KD and model compression in computer vision tasks. The specific teacher-student pairs or datasets used in this contribution (e.g., ResNet34→ResNet18 on ImageNet) are instances within the broader domain and do not constitute a new application area.
